key_insight: AtomSteer steers pretrained atomistic generative models toward chemical and crystallographic constraints at inference time, without retraining or architectural changes.
engineering_relevance: It adds structural control to existing workflows for crystal design, molecular conformer generation, and protein–ligand structure prediction while limiting disruption to generated geometry.
method: Correct intermediate predictions during sampling using bounded local projections.
Apply graph-rigid stereochemical transformations and periodic-symmetry projections.
Accept updates that improve constraint satisfaction while limiting changes elsewhere.
evidence_signal: Across FlowMM, ET-Flow, and Boltz-2, the abstract reports improved crystal symmetry coverage and recovery, molecular validity and E/Z accuracy, and fewer ligand E/Z errors with competitive docking success and PoseBusters validity.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify inference overhead or improvement magnitudes, leaving the practical cost–benefit trade-off unclear.
paper_title: AtomSteer: Test-Time Constraint Steering for Atomistic Generative Models
